title: Committee of Supply – Head L (Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head L (Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment)

sections.label: Net-zero emissions and carbon tax
sections.summary: The MSE GPC welcomes Singapore's commitment to achieve net-zero emissions sooner and to raise the carbon tax significantly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The MSE GPC is heartened to hear that Singapore will commit to achieve net-zero emissions sooner and will also raise the carbon tax significantly.

sections.label: Second-hand smoke in homes
sections.summary: In the past two months, 2,475 people approached the speaker for help with second-hand smoke in their own homes, almost 50% for over three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the past two months, 2,475 people in Singapore have approached me for help as they are suffering from second-hand smoke in their own homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What scares me is that almost 50% of them have been affected by second-hand smoke in their own homes for more than three years already.

sections.label: Charge for single-use carrier bags
sections.summary: Four years ago, in an Adjournment Motion, the speaker urged the Government to implement a charge for single-use carrier bags of all materials.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Four years ago, in an Adjournment Motion, I urged the Government to implement a charge for single-use carrier bags of all materials.

sections.label: Plastic bag charge for supermarkets
sections.summary: The speaker says using fewer plastic bags alone will not solve climate change but every bit counts, and asks why the charge is only for supermarkets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Using fewer plastic bags alone will not solve climate change or save the earth, but every bit counts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And making us conscious of our habits, and consider better alternatives, has value in itself.”  I am glad the Government announced that it will proceed with this charge but why only for supermarkets?

sections.label: Singapore plastic bag usage figures
sections.summary: Singapore uses 2.5 billion plastic bags a year, about 450 per person, and in 2019 and 2020 households and trade premises threw away 200,000 tonnes of disposables yearly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Chairman, when it comes to using plastic bags, Singapore is among the top.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We are using 2.5 billion plastic bags a year, according to NEA.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This can be translated to be about 450 plastic bags per person each year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And in 2019 and 2020, NEA pointed out households and trade premises in Singapore threw away 200,000 tonnes of disposables per year, two-thirds of which are disposable bags.

sections.label: Supermarket disposable carrier bag charge
sections.summary: MSE announced it would implement a disposable carrier bag charge at supermarkets, one of the recommendations of the Citizens Workgroup on Reducing the Excessive Consumption of Disposables.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: MSE has announced that it would implement a disposable carrier bag charge at supermarkets, which was one of the recommendations submitted by the Citizens Workgroup on Reducing the Excessive Consumption of Disposables.

sections.label: Charges for disposable carrier bags
sections.summary: Charges for disposable carrier bags in large supermarkets become a legal requirement in early 2023, following similar solutions in other countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Such a solution has already been implemented in various countries and generally attains success in reducing the usage of plastic bags.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We likewise hope to see a positive outcome in early 2023 when charges for disposable carriers bags in large supermarkets are made a legal requirement.

sections.label: E-waste Extended Producer Responsibility Scheme
sections.summary: The nationwide Extended Producer Responsibility Scheme for e-waste, implemented in July 2021, places greater responsibility on producers and retailers for end-of-life items.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With the implementation of the nationwide Extended Producer Responsibility Scheme for e-waste in July 2021, we have taken steps to regulate the disposal of such waste by placing greater responsibility on the producers and retailers of such products to ensure that the items ranging from our handphones to our light bulbs will be handled when they reach end of life.

sections.label: Zero Waste Masterplan recycling target
sections.summary: The Zero Waste Masterplan launched in 2019 sets a 2030 Domestic Recycling Rate target of 30%, after the rate declined from 19% in 2015 to 13% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, also on the Zero Waste Masterplan launched in 2019, our target for Domestic Recycling Rate in 2030 is 30%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is on the back of our domestic recycling rate declining from 19% in 2015 to 17% in 2019 and 13% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Their domestic recycling rate increased by almost 37% over just one decade.

sections.label: Coastal erosion defence structures
sections.summary: Walls and stone embankments covering 70% to 80% of Singapore's coastline have been erected to defend coastal areas from erosion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: To defend our coastal areas from erosion, we have erected walls and stone embankments covering 70% to 80% of Singapore's coastline.

sections.label: Sea wall construction timing
sections.summary: The passage asks when the construction of sea walls is expected to commence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: When do we expect the construction of sea walls to commence?

sections.label: Safeguarding low-lying areas
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister for an update on safeguarding low-lying areas against rising sea levels and whether protection studies can be sped up.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Can the Minister give an update on our progress to safeguard Singapore's low-lying areas against the threat of rising sea level?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Can the studies on the protection measures be speed up, so that it could mitigate the work needed to protect our shorelines?

sections.label: PUB drainage spending
sections.summary: PUB spent almost $2 billion on drainage in the last decade and plans $1.4 billion more in five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: To enhance flood resilience, PUB has spent almost $2 billion in the last decade and plans to spend $1.4 billion more in the next five years for drainage work.

sections.label: Singapore rising sea levels
sections.summary: Rising sea levels are a global challenge, and Singapore is vulnerable as a low-lying island with 30% of land five metres above sea level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Chairman, the rising sea levels is a global challenge for many coastal cities and Singapore is especially vulnerable, as we are a low-lying island with only 30% of our land residing five metres above sea level.

sections.label: Foreign vehicles emission law enforcement
sections.summary: Emission law violators must face the same consequences, and NEA should work with ICA to bar foreign vehicles until particulars or fines are settled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Those who violate our emission laws must face the same consequences, regardless of whether they are local or foreign drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I recommend that NEA work out an arrangement with ICA that will allow for measures; such as not allowing the foreign vehicles to be driven into or out of Singapore until such time the drivers' particulars are provided or the composition fine imposed for the commission of the offence is paid.

sections.label: WHO tobacco epidemic deaths
sections.summary: WHO says the tobacco epidemic kills over 8 million people yearly, with over 7 million from direct use and 1.2 million from second-hand smoke.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: According to WHO, the tobacco epidemic is one of the biggest public health threats the world has ever faced, killing more than 8 million people a year around the world.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: More than 7 million of those deaths are as a result of direct tobacco use while 1.2 million are the result of non-smokers being exposed to second-hand smoke.

sections.label: Tobacco bans and Orchard Road NSZ
sections.summary: New Zealand and Malaysia plan generational tobacco bans, and in 2019 Orchard Road became Singapore's first NSZ.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: New Zealand plans to raise the legal smoking age by one year every year, effectively banning the sales of tobacco products to people born after 2008.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Malaysia intends to introduce a new law to ban smoking and the possession of tobacco products, including electronic vaporisers, for people who are born after 2005, as a "Generational End Game" for smoking in the country.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: In 2019, the smoking prohibition was introduced and Orchard Road was designated Singapore’s first NSZ.

sections.label: Hawker centres transformation and cleanliness
sections.summary: Questions ask how the Hawker Centres Transformation Programme helps efficiency and sustainability, how many centres benefit, and about cleanliness and the Clean Tables Campaign.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: Can the Government share more details about how the Hawker Centres Transformation Programme is enabling hawker centres to be more efficient and sustainable, and how many hawker centres will benefit from this?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: How has hawker centre cleanliness improved over the past year, and does the Government have any preliminary findings on the effectiveness of the Clean Tables Campaign?

sections.label: Hawkers Succession Scheme progress
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry will share and update on the Hawkers Succession Scheme's progress in pairing retiring veteran hawkers with apprentices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: Will the Ministry share and update on the progress of the Hawkers Succession Scheme, which facilitates the pairing up of a retiring veteran hawker with an apprentice, so as to pass down his or her culinary skills, recipes and hawker stall to the aspiring successor?

sections.label: Hawkers Succession Scheme apprenticeship
sections.summary: NEA announced the Hawkers Succession Scheme, which aims to help retiring veteran hawkers pass down stalls, culinary skills, practices and recipes to aspiring successors through apprenticeship and mentorship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, we must ensure that our hawker culture and food continue to thrive for future generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am heartened to know that NEA has announced last year it will be rolling out the Hawkers Succession Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This scheme aims to facilitate retiring veteran hawkers pass down their stalls, culinary skills, practices and recipes to aspiring successors through an apprenticeship and mentorship programme.

sections.label: Animal agriculture land inefficiency
sections.summary: The Good Food Institute reports animal agriculture uses 77% of agricultural land for 17% of food supply, and plant-based meat emits less greenhouse gases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: According to the Good Food Institute, an international US-based non-profit re-imagining meat production, animal agriculture takes up 77% of all agricultural land on Earth despite supplying only 17% of humanity’s food supply.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: This inefficiency drives the need for agricultural expansion, which is the single largest driver for ecosystem damage on land.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: They reported that plant-based meat emits 30% to 90% less greenhouse gases than conventional meat production and animal agriculture contributes to more climate change than exhaust emissions from the entire transport sector.

sections.label: 30% local nutritional needs
sections.summary: One Government effort is to produce 30% of Singapore's nutritional needs locally and sustainably by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One of the Government's efforts to address this goal is to produce 30% of our nutritional needs locally and sustainably by 2030.

sections.label: SFA survey Singaporeans agree
sections.summary: An SFA survey found 98% of Singaporeans agree that this is an important effort.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: According to a survey done by SFA, 98% of Singaporeans agree that this is an important effort.

sections.label: 30 by 30 agri-food goal
sections.summary: The 30 by 30 goal aims to transform the agri-food sector and build capacity to grow productively, climate-resiliently and resource-efficiently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: One of the Government’s efforts is the 30 by 30 goal, to transform our agri-food sector, and build capabilities and capacity to sustainably grow in a highly productive, climate-resilient and resource-efficient way.

sections.label: Lim Chu Kang Master Plan status
sections.summary: The passage asks about the status of the Lim Chu Kang Master Plan exercise and the progress of discussions with the current cohort of farmers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee
sentences.text: What is the status of the Lim Chu Kang Master Plan exercise?

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee
sentences.text: What is the progress of the discussion with the current cohort of farmers?

sections.label: Desalinated water and NEWater share
sections.summary: Desalinated water and NEWater meet up to 70% of today's water demand, projected to reach 80% in 2030 and 85% by 2060.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Desalinated water and NEWater meet up to 70% of today's water demand and is projected to go up to 80% in 2030 and 85% by 2060.

sections.label: Tuas Nexus construction announcement
sections.summary: In September 2020, PUB and NEA announced construction of the Tuas Nexus, Singapore's first integrated water and solid waste management plant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In September 2020, PUB and NEA announced the construction of Singapore's first integrated water and solid waste management plant – the Tuas Nexus – consisting of the Tuas Water Reclamation Plant and the Integrated Management Facility.

sections.label: Deep Tunnel Sewerage System Phase Two
sections.summary: The passage asks whether PUB is on track to complete Deep Tunnel Sewerage System Phase Two, and notes water conservation targets and household study findings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: As a result of the pandemic situation, we know that many infrastructural projects have been affected due to manpower shortage and supply chain disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I, therefore, invite the Minister to share with this House, whether the PUB is on track to complete the Deep Tunnel Sewerage System Phase Two and an update on the progress of the project in the light of the present circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: PUB has placed emphasis on driving home the awareness on water conservation and set a target to achieve 130 litres usage per person per day by 2030 from the current 141 litres in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: In the 2018/2019 household study conducted by PUB, it showed that shower, flushing, kitchen and laundry constituted 77% of its total water usage and the consumption increased by 20% for households with domestic helpers.

sections.label: Waterless urinals and water taps
sections.summary: The passage suggests HDB consider purpose-built waterless urinals and other cleaning methods, and notes desalination and NEWater are weather resilient but energy intensive.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: For example, HDB to consider changing to purpose-built waterless urinal design for new flats, or using other methods to remove dirt from void decks and common corridors instead of high pressure water jets.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: I am glad we have over the years built alternate water taps like desalination and NEWater.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: They are weather resilient technologies, but equally energy intensive.

sections.label: Household water consumption during COVID-19
sections.summary: Household water consumption has increased as a result of COVID-19 due to people spending more time working from home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: Household water consumption has increased as a result of COVID-19 due to people spending more time working from home.

sections.label: IPCC report on extreme weather
sections.summary: The latest IPCC report states that climate change has increased the frequency and severity of extreme weather events, especially heat waves, droughts and floods.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The latest IPCC report underlines how climate change has resulted in increased frequency and severity of extreme weather events, especially heat waves, droughts, and floods.

sections.label: Zero Waste Masterplan targets
sections.summary: The Zero Waste Masterplan aims to cut carbon emissions, boost resource resilience and conserve landfill space, targeting a 30% reduction in waste-to-landfill per capita by 2030 and a 20% reduction by 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Our Zero Waste Masterplan was driven by the need to reduce carbon emissions, boost resource resilience and conserve landfill space.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We set a target to reduce waste-to-landfill per capita by 30% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Under the Singapore Green Plan, we will frontload efforts to achieve a 20% reduction by 2026.

sections.label: Consumer e-waste collection scheme
sections.summary: Since the scheme began in July last year, ALBA has collected around 3,500 tonnes of consumer e-waste, three times the annual amount under NEA's previous National Voluntary Partnership programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Since the scheme started in July last year, ALBA, the appointed scheme operator, has collected around 3,500 tonnes of consumer e-waste, which is three times the amount collected annually under NEA’s previous National Voluntary Partnership programme.

sections.label: Revised refuse disposal fees
sections.summary: The refuse disposal fee for incinerable waste will rise from $77 to $88 per tonne and for non-incinerable waste from $97 to $124 per tonne, effective 1 January 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: To keep pace with rising costs, we will revise the refuse disposal fee for incinerable waste from $77 to $88 per tonne.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: This fee is paid by public waste collectors and general waste collectors to dispose of incinerable waste at the waste-to-energy plants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We will also revise the refuse disposal fee for non-incinerable waste from $97 to $124 per tonne.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The revised fees will take effect on 1 January 2024, two years from now.

sections.label: Disposable carrier bag charge model
sections.summary: Last year it was announced that work would be done on an appropriate model for a disposable carrier bag charge at supermarkets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: After careful deliberation, we announced last year that we would work on an appropriate model for a disposable carrier bag charge at supermarkets.

sections.label: FairPrice No Plastic Bag initiative
sections.summary: FairPrice's "No Plastic Bag" initiative has saved more than 30 million plastic bags over two years, with seven out of 10 customers willing to bring their own bags.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: For example, FairPrice's "No Plastic Bag" initiative has saved more than 30 million plastic bags over two years, with seven out of 10 customers willing to bring their own bags.

sections.label: Supermarket bag charge consultation
sections.summary: About 6,000 stakeholders were consulted, and a charge of at least five cents per bag will apply at supermarket outlets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Close to 6,000 stakeholders were consulted through focus group discussions, industry and public consultation sessions and surveys.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling and Dr Lim also asked for details on the bag charge.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We will introduce a charge of at least five cents per bag for purchases made at the supermarket outlets.

sections.label: Bag charge scope and eligibility
sections.summary: Charging from the first bag encourages shoppers to bring their own bags, and applies to SFA-licensed supermarkets with turnover over $100 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Charging from the first bag would also encourage shoppers to bring their own bags from the outset.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: It will apply to operators of SFA-licensed supermarkets with an annual turnover of more than $100 million, which will cover about two thirds of all supermarket outlets.

sections.label: Supermarket bag charge accountability reporting
sections.summary: Supermarket operators must publish the number of bags issued, proceeds collected and how proceeds are used.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: To ensure accountability, we will require supermarket operators to publish information on the number of bags issued, amount of proceeds collected from the bag charge and how these proceeds would be used.

sections.label: Projected sea level rise
sections.summary: The Centre for Climate Research Singapore projected climate change could cause mean sea level rise of up to one metre by 2100.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The Centre for Climate Research Singapore has projected that climate change could cause mean sea level rise of up to one metre by 2100.

sections.label: Coastline site-specific studies
sections.summary: Site-specific studies are starting at other parts of the coastline, with JTC and PUB commencing studies at Jurong Island and the North West coast.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We are starting site-specific studies at other parts of our coastline.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: This year, JTC and PUB will commence studies at Jurong Island and the North West coast respectively.

sections.label: Coastal and flood protection funding
sections.summary: The Coastal and Flood Protection Fund was established in 2020 with five billion dollars, and SINGA allows loans for major long-term infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: To ensure that coastal and flood protection measures are adequately resourced, we established the Coastal and Flood Protection Fund in 2020 with an initial injection of five billion dollars.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: In May last year, the Government passed the Significant Infrastructure Government Loan Act (SINGA) to allow the raising of loans to finance major long-term infrastructure such as coastal and drainage infrastructure.

sections.label: Drainage improvement spending
sections.summary: Almost $2 billion was spent on drainage works since 2011, with $1.4 billion more set aside till 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The Government has invested significantly with almost $2 billion spent on drainage improvement works since 2011.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: This includes the Stamford Diversion Canal, Stamford Detention Tank and the Bukit Timah First Diversion Canal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We have set aside another $1.4 billion to carry out further improvements to the drainage system till 2025.

sections.label: PUB flood response vehicles
sections.summary: PUB expanded its fleet to 13 flood response vehicles that stream real-time flood conditions and drive through higher floodwaters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: PUB has also expanded its fleet to 13 flood response vehicles that are able to stream real-time flood conditions and drive through higher floodwaters.

sections.label: Hawker centre tray return rate
sections.summary: The national average Tray and Crockery Return Rate in hawker centres improved from 33% to 85% after the Clean Tables Campaign.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin would be pleased to know that since the Clean Tables Campaign and mandatory clean tables regime were implemented, the national average Tray and Crockery Return Rate (TCRR) in hawker centres has improved significantly, from 33% to 85%.

sections.label: Clean tables regime expansion
sections.summary: The clean tables regime will be implemented at another 2,700 premises this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Ms Hany Soh would be glad to hear that we will implement the regime at another 2,700 premises this year.

sections.label: Environmental Control Officers for large premises
sections.summary: Environmental Control Officers (Specified Premises) will be introduced for large premises, with 2,700 more ECCs and ECO(SP)s to be trained this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: For large premises with multiple tenants like shopping malls, Environmental Control Officers (Specified Premises) will be introduced to oversee more wide-ranging public health issues and management of stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We aim to train 2,700 more ECCs and ECO(SP)s this year.

sections.label: Smoking prohibition extension
sections.summary: NEA will extend smoking prohibition to remaining public parks, ABC Waters Sites and 10 beaches from 1 July 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Miss Cheryl Chan, Dr Lim Wee Kiak, Mr Louis Ng and Ms Poh Li San would be glad to hear that, together with PUB, NParks and the Sentosa Development Corporation, NEA will extend the smoking prohibition to more places including all remaining public parks and gardens, Active, Beautiful, Clean (ABC) Waters Sites and 10 beaches from 1 July 2022.

sections.label: Smoke-free shared recreational sites
sections.summary: Singaporeans can use shared recreational sites without second-hand smoke, with a three-month advisory before enforcement starts on 1 October 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: With this extension, Singaporeans can enjoy these shared recreational sites without exposure to second-hand tobacco smoke.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: There will be a three-month advisory period before enforcement commences on 1 October 2022.

sections.label: Study of New Zealand smoking ban
sections.summary: MOH remains open on end game smoking laws and will study New Zealand's ban, its effectiveness and applicability to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: On "end game" laws for smoking, MOH remains open and will study how New Zealand implements the ban, its effectiveness and how their experience could be applicable to Singapore.

sections.label: Surveillance and lab testing expansion
sections.summary: Since February 2022, surveillance covers 440 sites, including 150 in residential areas and town centres, and lab capacity rose to 4,000 samples weekly from 2,500.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Since February 2022, we have achieved surveillance coverage of 440 sites, including 150 sites distributed across residential areas and town centres.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We have also expanded our laboratory testing capacity to 4,000 samples being tested per week, up from 2,500 in July last year.

sections.label: Grant for SFA-licensed food operators
sections.summary: SFA-licensed operators and stallholders in markets, hawker centres, coffee shops, food courts and canteens receive $1,000 per local employee with mandatory CPF contributions, capped at $10,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: SFA-licensed operators and stallholders in markets, hawker centres, coffee shops, food courts and canteens will receive this grant.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: They will receive $1,000 for each local employee receiving mandatory CPF contributions, capped at $10,000.

sections.label: Cooked food stallholders online and e-payment
sections.summary: About half of over 6,000 cooked food stallholders are on board these services, and almost 70% have adopted e-payment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Currently, about half of our 6,000 plus cooked food stallholders are on board these services, and almost 70% of them have adopted e-payment.

sections.label: HTP pilot and hawker stall demand
sections.summary: HTP applies to new and redeveloped centres and is piloted at two existing centres, with 2022 consultation on Geylang Serai and Cheng San; hawker stall occupancy averages about 97%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: While HTP will be applied to new and redeveloped centres, we are also piloting it at two existing centres even as they face constraints with limited floor space.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that we will consult stakeholders, including Hawkers’ Associations, Town Councils and Advisers in 2022 to jointly develop the HTP pilot at Geylang Serai Market and Cheng San Market and Food Centre.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: On Mr Don Wee’s query, there has been healthy demand for hawker stalls, with high occupancy rates averaging consistently at about 97% at existing and new hawker centres.

sections.label: New hawkers joining trade
sections.summary: Over 40 new hawkers have joined the trade through these programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Over 40 new hawkers have joined the trade through these programmes.

sections.label: Veteran hawker stipend
sections.summary: Veteran hawkers will receive a nominal stipend of up to $5,500 in recognition of their time and effort.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: In recognition of their time and effort spent, veteran hawkers will receive a nominal stipend of up to $5,500.

sections.label: Four new hawker centres
sections.summary: Four new centres, Bukit Canberra, Fernvale, One Punggol and Senja Hawker Centres, will begin operations by the third quarter of this year despite COVID-19 delays.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: While COVID-19 has caused some delay, four new centres – namely Bukit Canberra, Fernvale, One Punggol and Senja Hawker Centres, will begin operations by the third quarter of this year.

sections.label: New centres and Market Street
sections.summary: All new centres will have food waste digesters, and Market Street Hawker Centre will open from 1 April at CapitaSpring levels two and three.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: All new centres will have food waste digesters.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Market Street Hawker Centre that used to be at Golden Shoe Carpark will open for business from 1 April, at levels two and three of the integrated development CapitaSpring on Market Street and continue to provide affordable food options for those working in the CBD.

sections.label: Smoking ban in parks
sections.summary: From 1 Jul 2022, smoking will be banned at Regional and City Parks and the park connector system linking various parks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: From 1 Jul 2022, we will ban smoking at Regional and City Parks like East Coast Park and Fort Canning Park, as well as the park connector system linking various parks.

sections.label: CPF payment incentive
sections.summary: For every employee operators and stallholders pay CPF for, they will receive $1,000, capped at a maximum of $10,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: For every employee that operators and stallholders pay CPF for, they will receive $1,000, capped at a maximum of $10,000.

sections.label: Four hawker centres opening
sections.summary: Four hawker centres will be opened this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: In addition, we will be opening four hawker centres this year.

sections.label: MSE food supply resilience
sections.summary: MSE plans to ensure food supply resilience through three food baskets: diversify import sources, grow local and grow overseas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: MSE plans to ensure food supply resilience through our three food baskets – diversify import sources, grow local and grow overseas.

sections.label: Singapore Food Story R&D Programme
sections.summary: Up to $144 million was set aside for R&D, with around $75 million committed to over 30 projects to date.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Under the Singapore Food Story R&D Programme, we set aside up to $144 million for R&D for sustainable urban food production, future foods, such as advanced biotech-based protein production, as well as food safety science and innovation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: To date, around $75 million has been committed to over 30 projects.

sections.label: Leases for sea-based farms
sections.summary: Sea-based farms will be offered leases in the longer term, starting with yearly-renewable temporary occupation licences from 1 January 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Today, sea-based farms do not have a lease mechanism and this creates some uncertainty for our farms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: So, we will offer leases to all sea-based farms in the longer term.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Incumbent farms will be eased into this arrangement by starting with yearly-renewable temporary occupation licences (TOL) from 1 January 2023.

sections.label: Extending farm leases
sections.summary: Future tenders will offer farmers the option to extend their lease beyond 20 years for an additional 10 years, subject to SFA production output conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: To address Ms Nadia Samdin, Prof Koh Lian Pin and Mr Raj Joshua Thomas' queries, we want to provide greater certainty for our farmers so that they will invest more into their farms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: This means that future tenders will offer farmers the option of extending their lease beyond the initial 20-year period for an additional 10 years, subject to the farms meeting SFA’s production output conditions.

sections.label: Agri-Food Cluster Transformation Fund
sections.summary: SFA received 32 ACT Fund applications as of end of last year, approved eight, and will expand the fund's scope.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Last year, I shared that SFA launched a $60 million Agri-Food Cluster Transformation (ACT) Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: SFA has received a total of 32 applications as of end of last year and eight applications have already been approved, while the rest are being processed and evaluated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Going forward, we will also expand the scope of the ACT fund to allow more food types that are commonly consumed in Singapore to also benefit from higher co-funding quantum.

sections.label: Food imports and local production
sections.summary: Singapore will keep importing most food and any shift between imports and local production will result from market forces.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Even as we aim to produce more food locally, Singapore will continue to need to import most of our food.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: We remain committed to facilitating free, open and competitive trade, and any substitution between imports and local production will be a result of market forces.

sections.label: Long-term leases for sea-based farms
sections.summary: Long-term leases will be offered to all sea-based farms, starting with yearly renewable temporary occupation licences from 1 January 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: After the reviewing the policy on the lease of sea space, I am glad to announce that we will offer long-term leases to all sea-based farms to help attract investors to develop the local aquaculture industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: To help existing farms ease into this arrangement, we will start with yearly renewable temporary occupation licences from 1 January 2023.

sections.label: Water security and Jurong Island desalination
sections.summary: Water security will be strengthened with weather-resilient sources, and the Jurong Island Desalination Plant will be operational in April 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Chairman, I would now like to speak about our other basic need, which is water.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: We will continue to strengthen water security by developing weather-resilient sources like NEWater and desalinated water and I am happy to announce that Singapore’s latest plant, Jurong Island Desalination Plant, will be operational in Apr 2022.

sections.label: Energy for desalinated water
sections.summary: The energy to produce one cubic metre of desalinated water could fall from 3.5 to under two kilowatt hours by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: The energy to produce one cubic metre of desalinated water could, potentially, be reduced from 3.5 kilowatt hours to less than two kilowatt hours by 2025.

sections.label: IWMF excess electricity to grid
sections.summary: When fully operational, the IWMF's excess electricity exported to the grid can power up to 300,000 four-room HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: When fully operational, the excess electricity exported to the grid by IWMF will be able to power up to 300,000 four-room HDB flats.

sections.label: National Action Strategy on Marine Litter
sections.summary: The Government is on track to publish Singapore's first National Action Strategy on Marine Litter in June 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: Beyond our local waterways, we are also inspiring collective action to safeguard our marine environment from the threats posed by marine litter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: I am pleased to update Ms Nadia Samdin that the Government is on track to publish Singapore's first National Action Strategy on Marine Litter in June 2022.

sections.label: Water consumption changes
sections.summary: In 2021 non-domestic water consumption fell 6% while domestic rose 6%, with household use rising from 141 to 158 litres per day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: In 2021, non-domestic water consumption fell by 6% while domestic water consumption increased by 6% compared to the pre-COVID-19 period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: In per capita terms, household water consumption increased from 141 litres per day in 2019, to 158 litres per day in 2021.

sections.label: Smart water meters and idling engines
sections.summary: PUB began phase one in Tampines Central in January 2022, installing 300,000 smart water meters by 2023, and the idling engine proposal will be studied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: PUB has commenced the roll-out of the first phase of the programme in Tampines Central in January 2022 and will be installing some 300,000 smart water meters in new and existing residential, commercial and industrial premises, target to complete by 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: I also want to thank Mr Murali for his suggestion to plug the existing gaps with enforcing foreign vehicles that have idling engines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: There are practical challenges, but I want to assure Mr Murali that we will be studying this proposal.

sections.label: Plastic bags and smoking prohibition
sections.summary: The change is needed to cultivate habits, legislation is kept open pending response, and smoking prohibition is monitored for extension.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Having thought through all the considerations and also positions that we have taken in the past about how relevant plastic bags are in our daily lives, we need to make this change, it is important for us start cultivating that habit and let us see what happens after that.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: When you have that as part of your habits, then I think we do not need to use the lever of legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, I am keeping it open for now.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We will see what is the response by the people and by the business community, and we will review it over time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: With regard to a roadmap, as I have said before, we continue to monitor and review if we can further extend our smoking prohibition from time to time.

sections.label: Calibrating sector requirements
sections.summary: Working with the sector to calibrate requirements can reduce or avoid downstream costs such as gastroenteritis cases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, what we really have done, as I have said is to work with the sector and calibrate the requirements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: And if you think about it, if you do it right upstream, actually it will help you to reduce or avoid costs downstream because it will avoid, say gastroenteritis cases or minimise or reduce the cases.

sections.label: Profiteering and bag charges
sections.summary: Even without the latest legislation proposal, some shops already collect a bag charge for environmental reasons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: On the first point about possibility of profiteering, right now, even without this latest legislation proposal, some shops are already collecting a bag charge for environmental reasons.

sections.label: Applying proceeds to causes
sections.summary: Applying proceeds to environmental and social causes is mandatory, but supermarket operators choose how, such as through CSR and ESG programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Second point about whether we would make it mandatory to apply their proceeds to environmental and social causes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The answer is yes, but we are not requiring them to put it into specific charities or specific causes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The supermarket operators will have the choice of how they want to apply, maybe as part of their CSR and ESG programme.

sections.label: SFA technology and regulations
sections.summary: SFA will keep abreast with latest technology and review regulations to keep pace with developments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: The short answer to the Member is yes, SFA will continue to keep abreast with the latest technology and also review our regulations to keep pace with what is coming up.

sections.label: Slowing water and drainage investment
sections.summary: All ways to slow water movement will be used, with significant investment over the next few years to improve drainage including Bukit Timah.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Really, all ways to slow down the movement of water.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We are going to invest significantly over the next few years in order to improve our drainage system, including Bukit Timah.

sections.label: Flood-prone areas and carbon pricing
sections.summary: Some areas have become more flood-prone as water moves to the lowest point, and a single flood event cannot be prevented; countries have adopted carbon pricing for net zero by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, we are starting to see some areas that did not used to be flood-prone have now becoming more flood-prone partly because we have already worked on some areas and, therefore, the water will its way towards the lowest point now and we have to continue to improve our infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: But more importantly is that we cannot prevent the possibility of a single flood event in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: In the pursuit of meeting net zero emissions by 2050, several countries have adopted carbon pricing to different extent, with this mechanism likely to be a global norm in time to come.

sections.label: Tiered carbon tax for households
sections.summary: A possible mechanism is for power generation companies to tier carbon tax passed to households by usage, with the first 400 kilowatt hour having no carbon tax passed on.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: A possible mechanism that I can suggest could be on the power generation companies to tier the cost being passed down to households based on usage, for example, with the first 400 kilowatt hour having no carbon tax passed on, and a subsequent tier percentage to be determined by the Energy Market Authority of the carbon tax allowable to be passed on for every 100 kilowatt hour thereafter.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: This would ensure that the households that are conserving energy and using electricity within the national average level are not penalised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Due to our lack of renewable energy resources, we may only be able to meet the net-zero target by or around 2050, as we avail of new opportunities in the carbon market and technological breakthroughs.

sections.label: Revised NDCs to UNFCC
sections.summary: The question asks what Singapore's revised Nationally Determined Contributions to be submitted to UNFCC in 2022 are.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: What are our revised Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) to be submitted to UNFCC in 2022?

sections.label: International carbon credits and accountability
sections.summary: From 2024 businesses can use high-quality international carbon credits to offset up to 5% of taxable emissions, and the question asks about accountability measures and the Government's net-zero target.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: From 2024, businesses will be able to use and I quote, "high-quality international carbon credits to offset up to 5% of their taxable emissions." What accountability measures will the Government put in place to ensure transparency and fair implementation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: How much of the Government's own net- zero target will be based on such international carbon credit offsets?

sections.label: Net-zero target and public consultations
sections.summary: Public consultations will be done as part of revising Singapore's Nationally Determined Contributions and net-zero target.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, in line with Singapore's announcement of our revised target to achieve net-zero emissions by or around 2050 and the review of Singapore's Nationally Determined Contributions by COP27, the Finance Minister mentioned in his Budget 2022 speech that public consultations will be done as part of this revision and review.

sections.label: How carbon offsets work
sections.summary: Credible carbon offsets require payment to reduce total emissions, with funds buying and retiring carbon permits.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: So, go on, do the math quickly in your head.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Now, making carbon offsets that truly work requires that the amount paid for said offsets actually goes toward reducing the total amount of carbon emitted into the atmosphere.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Recall, carbon cap-and-trade systems are typically seeded with a fixed amount of carbon emissions distributed via permits.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Hence, a credible exchange would direct the funds from the carbon offset toward the purchase of permits, which are then retired from circulation.

sections.label: Carbon offsets for official travel
sections.summary: MSE is suggested to require credible carbon offsets for all official international travel by civil servants.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To this end, I would like to suggest that MSE consider requiring the purchase of credible carbon offsets along the lines of what I have described for all official international travel by civil servants.

sections.label: Carbon credits and net-zero
sections.summary: MSE is asked to explain how globally traded carbon credits can help Singapore reach net-zero.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Can MSE explain on the specifics on how these globally traded carbon credits can help us reach net-zero?

sections.label: Carbon tax level and increments
sections.summary: Government is asked how revised carbon tax levels support green transition and affect households and businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee
sentences.text: Would the Government elaborate on how the revised carbon tax level and any potential increments will support our green transition and what is the expected impact on households and businesses?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: Chairman, Singapore’s carbon tax will be progressively increased to reach S$50 to S$80 per tonne of emissions by 2030, so that we will meet our new target of reaching net-zero by or around 2050.

sections.label: Minimising carbon tax impact on consumers
sections.summary: Government is asked how it would minimise carbon tax impact on middle- and lower-income consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: How would the Government help to minimise the impact of the carbon tax on consumers, especially those in the middle- and lower-income groups?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: This covers around 50 facilities that contribute to about 80% of our total carbon emissions.

sections.label: Waste incineration capacity limit
sections.summary: At the current rate of waste incineration, the site is expected to be full by 2035.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: At the current rate of waste incineration, it is expected to be full by 2035.

sections.label: Closing the Resource Loop initiative
sections.summary: NEA has been administering the $45 million Closing the Resource Loop funding initiative on sustainable resource recovery solutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: NEA has been administering the $45 million Closing the Resource Loop funding initiative on sustainable resource recovery solutions.

sections.label: Budget 2022 net-zero commitment
sections.summary: Finance Minister Lawrence Wong committed to raising the net-zero emissions goal and increasing the carbon tax rate toward $50 to $80 per tonne by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: More recently, in his Budget 2022 speech, Finance Minister Lawrence Wong committed to raising our goal of achieving net-zero emissions by or around mid-century and increasing our carbon tax rate with a view to reaching $50 to $80 per tonne by 2030.

sections.label: Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 Plan
sections.summary: The Government announced the $25 billion RIE2025 Plan for 2021 to 2025, with $5.2 billion to scale up innovation and enterprise platforms.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin
sentences.text: In December 2020, the Government announced its Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 Plan (RIE2025), amounting to $25 billion allocated for the period 2021 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin
sentences.text: The Government also mentioned that we will allocate $5.2 billion under RIE2025 to scale up innovation and enterprise platforms, including those seeking to facilitate research and technology translation.

sections.label: Companies tapping energy efficiency funds
sections.summary: Given the revised carbon tax trajectory, more Singapore-based companies can be expected to tap funds such as the Energy Efficiency Fund.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin
sentences.text: Given the revised carbon tax trajectory in Budget 2022, we can expect more Singapore-based companies to tap into funds, such as the Energy Efficiency Fund, to improve energy efficiency of their operations as part of their decarbonisation journey.

sections.label: SG Eco Fund grant calls
sections.summary: With $50 million set aside, the SG Eco Fund has held two grant calls, awarding almost $4 million to 79 projects.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: Chairman, with $50 million set aside in total, the SG Eco Fund has had two grant calls so far, awarding almost $4 million to 79 projects – no small amount to show our commitment to the environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: These funds have supported a wide range of projects from community-based scavenger hunts to a freshwater mangrove wetland development project, among many others.

sections.label: Earmarked eco towns
sections.summary: The Government had earmarked Choa Chu Kang, Nee Soon and Tampines as eco towns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee
sentences.text: Chairman, the Government had earmarked Choa Chu Kang, Nee Soon and Tampines as eco towns.

sections.label: Very hot days increase
sections.summary: Very hot days with real feel temperature above 40 degrees have increased about eight times since the 1950s to over 80 days yearly, and an urban heat action plan is being worked on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The number of very hot days where the real feel temperature, considering humidity, exceeds 40 degrees has increased by about eight times since the 1950s to over 80 days each year now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government mentioned one year ago that it is working on an urban heat impact mitigation action plan.

sections.label: Green Towns Programme prioritisation
sections.summary: The Green Towns Programme does not prioritise vulnerable neighbourhoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: From what I understand, the Green Towns Programme does not prioritise vulnerable neighbourhoods.

sections.label: Living space temperature requirements
sections.summary: The speaker asks about including living space temperature requirements under building control regulations and about targets to retrofit all estates for the urban heat island effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Moreover, can we look into including living space temperature requirements under the building control regulations?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I would also like to ask what are the Government's targets to retrofit all estates to deal with the urban heat island effect?

sections.label: Businesses sustainability help
sections.summary: Businesses need to be brought up to speed on sustainability and helped to assess gaps and develop net zero plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One, at the company level, our businesses need to be brought up to speed on the what and the how of sustainability and they need help to assess their gaps and develop the plans that will take them to net zero.

sections.label: Financial hub carbon trading
sections.summary: The country's trusted status as a financial hub positions it as a potential key player in carbon trading.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At a country level, our trusted status as a financial hub land ourselves as a potential key player in carbon trading.

sections.label: Financial support for green transition
sections.summary: Financial support for green transition is critical for businesses as they map out their net zero plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Next, financial support for green transition is critical for businesses as they map out their net zero plans.

sections.label: Tax incentives for SMEs
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government can consider targeted tax incentives or rebates to SMEs for their sustainability adoption progress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Government consider providing targeted tax incentives or rebates to SMEs as a measure of their progress in their sustainability adoption?

sections.label: Singapore support for green economy
sections.summary: Asks what support and investments Singapore has made and will make for green economy business growth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: What support and investments has Singapore made and will make to support the growth of businesses in the green economy in areas such as green ICT, carbon services and trading hub and goods and services related to low-carbon project development, project financing, trading, consultancy and measurement, reporting and verification?

sections.label: Green public procurement buying power
sections.summary: Public sector procurement causes 15% of global greenhouse gas emissions, and green public procurement can boost the green economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Globally, public sector procurement activities are directly or indirectly responsible for 15% of global greenhouse gas emissions – seven times the amount emitted by the entire aviation industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: They are also heavily concentrated in six industries: defence and security, transportation, waste management services, construction, industrial products and utilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Using this buying power, green public procurement can be a major boost for the green economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Government can set standards for products, services and project activities, certify companies and materials for sustainability, giving extra points for suppliers that are "greener".

sections.label: Government levers for decarbonisation
sections.summary: Lists government levers including funding for R&D, industry coalitions, data systems, market adoption incentives and education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Other levers for the Government include funding and incentives for innovation and R&D in transformative new technologies, working with industry coalitions to promote decarbonisation across the value chains, upgrading and making available climate and sustainability data and analytics systems, providing incentives for market adoption such as low interest loans and tax credits and boosting understanding expertise and capabilities through education and reskilling programs, the subject of my next cut.

sections.label: Green Bonds and local firms
sections.summary: Green Bonds provide capital for sustainable developments, and asks how green local firms can be part of RIE2025 investment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: The issuance of Green Bonds will provide a substantial capital base for sustainable developments not only in Singapore, but also throughout the region.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: It is critical that in our drive for sustainability, we fully leverage this opportunity to groom a new generation of green local firms, support them to build their green capabilities and position them to capture emerging opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Minister what can be done to ensure that the development of green local firms is an integral part of the $25 billion investment under RIE2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: We should consider a special programme, with R&D funding to be carved out, especially to support and promote development of green technologies and solutions by our very own local firms and startups.

sections.label: Reshare terms for lending
sections.summary: Government provides 70% reshare to catalyse lending by participating financial institutions, and industry calls for more favourable terms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: With the Government providing 70% of reshare to catalyse lending by participating financial institutions, there have been calls by the industry for more favourable terms, such as preferential interest rate and loan terms, in order to spur adoption.

sections.label: Nikkei carbon credit investigation
sections.summary: A Nikkei investigation found that more carbon credits were issued than it could likely make good on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A Nikkei investigation found that more carbon credits were issued than it could likely make good on.

sections.label: Sustainability sector talent plans
sections.summary: Questions ask about Government plans for industry-ready sustainability talents and whether IHLs provide adequate training and upskilling.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What are the Government's plans for building a Singapore core of industry-ready talents to support our emerging sustainability sector, especially in relation to our Industry Transformation Maps?

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Has the Ministry assessed whether our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) provide adequate training and upskilling programmes on sustainability-related competencies at the undergraduate, graduate and continuing education levels, to address talent gaps in our emerging sustainability sector?

sections.label: Carbon credits offsetting taxable emissions
sections.summary: Allowing businesses to use high-quality carbon credits to offset up to 5% of taxable emissions will help stimulate local demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While the Government's decision to allow businesses to use high-quality carbon credits to offset up to 5% of the taxable emissions will help stimulate local demand for such credits, as with many other things, we must also look to cater to external demand.

sections.label: Carbon credit trading ecosystem update

sentences.text: What about lorries, buses, and coaches and other heavy-duty vehicles?

sentences.text: In 2021, Singapore's population of electric cars more than doubled from 1,217 to 2,942 cars.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin
sentences.text: Buildings account for over 20% of our carbon emissions.

sections.summary: HDB envisages the Green Towns Programme as a 10-year plan to reduce energy consumption, recycle rainwater and cool the built environment in HDB towns.

sentences.text: Mr Chairman, HDB envisages the Green Towns Programme as a 10‐year plan that aims to reduce energy consumption, recycle rainwater and cool the built environment in all HDB towns.

sections.label: Local food growing community efforts
sections.summary: To support growing 30% of local nutritional needs by 2030, the Ministry should encourage community efforts like growing edible plants in households and housing estates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, to support our goal of growing 30% of our local nutritional needs by 2030, the Ministry should encourage more local community efforts, such as growing small edible plants in households and available plots in housing estates.

sections.label: HDB full-glass windows heat

sentences.text: Many of our existing HDB flats comprise full-glass windows that transfer considerable amounts of heat through the afternoon sun.

sections.label: City in Nature plans

sentences.text: Two years ago, MND announced its plans to transform our green landscape even further, turning Singapore into a “City in Nature”.

sentences.text: This includes dedicating another 200 hectares of nature parks by 2030 and having 300 kilometres of Nature Ways and 500 kilometres of park connectors by 2030.

sections.label: Southern Islands visitorship increase

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Furthermore, visitorship to our Southern Islands increased by 20% to 30% in 2020 and they are being promoted as a good escape from the city.

sections.label: Sustainability competencies in curriculum
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government has considered adding sustainability competencies and systems level thinking to the education curriculum so learners are equipped for a global green economy.

sentences.text: Has the Government considered incorporating sustainability competencies and systems level thinking into our education curriculum at appropriate levels to ensure that our learners are well-equipped for a global green economy and will be ready to compete with global talent?

sentences.text: The inaugural Skills Demand for the Future Economy report has identified more than 450 green job roles across 17 sectors, ranging from manufacturing and trade and connectivity, to financial services and the built environment.

sentences.text: Can the Ministry please share what efforts the IHLs are undertaking to further support the green economy and sustainable living?

sections.label: New sustainability courses at universities
sections.summary: New courses on sustainability are being launched at NUS and other Autonomous Universities, and carbon tax will be deployed as the rate rises to $50 to $80 per tonne.

sentences.text: New courses at NUS include a Major in Sustainable Urban Development, which "aims to train the next generation of urban problem-solvers".

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: In the years to come, a significant amount of carbon tax will be deployed as Singapore progressively raises the carbon tax rate to $50 to $80 per tonne of emissions.

sections.label: Singapore's 2030 NDC and LEDS
sections.summary: Two years ago Singapore submitted its enhanced 2030 NDC and Long-Term Low Emissions Development Strategy under the Paris Agreement.

sentences.text: Two years ago, Singapore submitted our enhanced Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) for 2030, and our Long-Term Low Emissions Development Strategy (LEDS) under the Paris Agreement – to halve emissions from our 2030 peak to 33 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent by 2050, with a view to achieving net-zero emissions as soon as viable in the second half of the century.

sections.label: Raising ambition to net-zero

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: With these important developments, we are now able to have greater clarity and to raise our ambition to achieve net-zero emissions by or around mid-century, in line with the Glasgow Climate Pact.

sections.label: Reviewing 2030 NDC and LEDS

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: We will then declare and make a formal revision to both our NDC and LEDS later this year.

sections.label: COP26 carbon market rules
sections.summary: The rules were among the most difficult negotiations at COP26 and lay the foundation for credible carbon markets and reporting clarity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: This was one of the most difficult negotiations in COP26.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: These rules lay the foundation for rigorous, robust and credible carbon markets and provide clarity on environmental integrity and accounting by buyer and seller countries when reporting their national emissions.

sections.label: Energy transition and RIE decarbonisation funding

sections.label: COP26 net-zero private capital pledge

sentences.text: At COP26, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero, a coalition of 450 financial firms representing some 40% of global banking assets, pledged to make over S$170 trillion of private capital available for investment to reach global net-zero by 2050.

sentences.text: Our proposed carbon tax out to 2030 is set at a level that sends a significant price signal to influence consumer and business behaviour.

sentences.text: The International Energy Agency estimates that, to match their targets, China and South Korea would have carbon prices of S$45 and S$61 per tonne respectively in 2030.

sections.label: Climate-Friendly Household Package registration

sections.label: Green Plan ministries and net-zero move
sections.summary: Green Plan Ministries gathered at COS to explain enhanced initiatives, and the passage calls for a collective move to net-zero with costs and trade-offs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: We can and we should make this decisive move to net-zero.

sentences.text: We must advance on this sustainability journey together as a nation and we will require the participation and support of all Singaporeans to do so.

sentences.text: There will be costs to bear and trade-offs to be made.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean

sentences.text: NEA and PUB launched the Climate-Friendly Households Programme in 2020 to help 1-room to 3-room HDB households reduce energy and water consumption.
